questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why Latin is no longer spoken today
Languages that people have invented
How to learn a language through TV shows
Why English grammar is so hard to learn
questions.why: They discuss invented languages such as Klingon, Dothraki, Saint Hildegard's language and Esperanto.

questions.q: Why is Neil confused at the start of the programme?
options: Sam speaks to him in Klingon
Sam doesn't answer his question at all
Sam says she is ill and must go home
Sam says she's fine, then adds 'not'
questions.why: Sam says 'I'm fine… not!' – using 'not' at the end to mean the opposite of what she said.

questions.q: Why do small changes like 'my bad' happen in English?
options: People use it in their daily lives
Teachers invent new words every year
It copies words from Latin
TV shows create new grammar rules
questions.why: Neil says unlike Latin, English is a living language – people speak and use it in their ordinary lives.

questions.q: Why was the Klingon language created?
options: To help people from different countries talk
As a university research project
For alien characters in the TV show Star Trek
To be used in songs by a Dutch opera company
questions.why: When Star Trek introduced alien characters called Klingons, the makers needed a whole new language.

questions.q: Why doesn't David Peterson think Saint Hildegard's creation was a proper language?
options: Because it was only used in one small church
Because nobody could understand her songs
Because it had no new words of its own
She made new nouns but used Latin grammar
questions.why: He says she had a list of nouns but used Latin grammar, and a language is not just vocabulary.

questions.q: Why did Ludwik Zamenhof invent Esperanto?
options: To help people who spoke different languages
To write a new kind of fantasy story for TV
To replace Latin in all European schools
To create a secret language for doctors
questions.why: Sam says he wanted to make it easier for people who spoke different languages to communicate.

questions.q: How did Michael Rosen understand the word 'parolas'?
options: He had studied Esperanto at school
David Peterson explained it to him
He guessed it from its Latin root
He looked it up in a dictionary
questions.why: Michael says he got 'the parle bit from its Latin root'.

questions.q: What happened when David Peterson said a second sentence in Esperanto?
options: Michael understood it immediately
Michael couldn't work out what it meant
Michael answered in Esperanto
Michael said it sounded like Klingon
questions.why: Michael guessed 'Who is my father?' and 'Where am I travelling?' before saying 'I got stuck on that one!'
